claims.text: The canonical, JSON-safe view -- the thing that gets digested.
claims.why: The method returns a dict with JSON-safe types (str, list, dict).

claims.text: Preserve every legacy TaskSpec digest/effect key byte-for-byte.
claims.why: Legacy keys are not shown in this chunk; cannot verify preservation.

claims.text: There is no ``repo_root`` field, and that absence is load-bearing: a runner that cannot name the primary checkout cannot write it by accident.
claims.why: The dataclass fields listed (worktree, branch, base_revision, task, is_cancelled) do not include repo_root.

claims.text: A gate verdict on candidate code is only worth as much as the boundary it ran behind, so the boundary that ACTUALLY held travels with the verdict into the ledger.
claims.why: The comment references ContainmentAttestation and ledger; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The trimmed view written to the ledger (see GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS).
claims.why: GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``diff_bytes`` is authoritative and ``diff_sha256`` is taken over it; a human promoting the patch should write those bytes, not the decoded ``diff``, because a decode round-trip can corrupt a diff containing bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
claims.why: The class has diff_bytes, diff_sha256, and diff property decodes with 'replace', confirming diff_bytes is authoritative.

claims.text: Convenience view for humans and logs; not the digested form.
claims.why: Property returns decoded string; class has diff_sha256 for digestion.

claims.text: True only for a real, gated candidate. ``no_change`` is not ok.
claims.why: STATE_CLEAN is not defined in this chunk; cannot confirm mapping.

claims.text: JSON-safe view. Carries the gate SUMMARY, not the full log.
claims.why: to_dict includes gates.summary() (which is trimmed) not full output.

claims.text: The gate command line, as a pure function so it is assertable.
claims.why: Function takes paths and returns tuple; no side effects visible.

claims.text: ``-p no:cacheprovider`` keeps pytest from writing ``.pytest_cache`` into the candidate worktree; the patch is captured before gates run, but a gate that dirties the tree it is judging is a trap worth not setting.
Delete the gate's scratch directory through the GUARDED walker.
claims.why: remove_tree_no_follow is not defined in this chunk; cannot confirm it is guarded.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` on success, or a one-line report of what stopped it.
claims.why: Function returns None on success, or a formatted error string on exception.

claims.text: Poll one gate child, honouring the cancel token and the deadline.
claims.why: Function polls proc.poll(), checks ctx.is_cancelled() and time.monotonic() against deadline.
Function returns (cancelled, timed_out, proc.poll()) after loop.

claims.text: POLLING RATHER THAN READING IS WHY OUTPUT GOES TO A FILE.
claims.why: No file output setup visible in this chunk; output destination not shown.

claims.text: Shared by both spawn paths so the contained and uncontained children are cancelled by the same code -- a second copy is a second place for that deadlock to reappear.

observations.what: TaskSpec.body includes conditional fields based on presence of self attributes
RunnerContext does not have repo_root field, as documented
GateResult.containment is typed with a forward reference (string) to ContainmentAttestation
GateResult.summary uses GATE_OUTPUT_TAIL_CHARS which is not defined in this chunk
PatchArtifact.diff uses decode with 'replace' which can silently corrupt non-UTF-8 bytes
AttemptResult.ok checks state against STATE_CLEAN which is not defined in this chunk
_remove_gate_tmpdir calls remove_tree_no_follow which is not imported or defined in this chunk
_poll_until_done calls proc.cancel() which is not a standard subprocess method
_poll_until_done returns proc.poll() after loop; if loop exits without poll being None, returncode is set
